page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9it.large is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Enhanced ecs.g9it instance family. Built on KVM virtualization and standard x86_64 architecture, this instance integrates an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The compute configuration delivers 2 dedicated vCPUs backed by 8.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per virtual core.

The instance relies exclusively on network-attached block storage, providing 0 GB of local storage. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Acceleration hardware is not included, featuring zero GPUs. Additionally, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default, requiring separate external network resource allocation when public access is needed.

This hardware footprint provides a cost-efficient profile for moderate application tiers that do not demand expansive local drive caches or extreme parallel processing. With dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory provisioning, it suits workloads including small-scale web serving, microservices, continuous integration tasks, lightweight enterprise software, and mid-tier backend processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9it.large is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine within the Enhanced ecs.g9it instance family. Operating on the KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, offering a balanced 1:4 resource ratio with 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance features no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent workloads, and includes a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile without bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With dedicated compute cores and standard memory density, it delivers a cost-efficient resource environment suited for mid-sized general workloads including lightweight web serving, microservice hosting, development environments, and small enterprise backend components.
